standard_prerequisites.name: Henselization and strict henselization of a local ring, and the residue field of the strict henselization
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at statement lines 31346-31347 and proof lines 31384-31388
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the rings whose spectra are compared and supplies the identification of the residue field with kappa^{sep}.

standard_prerequisites.name: The integral closure of a reduced local ring in its total ring of fractions as a finite product of normal domains
standard_prerequisites.use: Is what makes every local ring of (A')^{sh} a normal domain and hence gives uniqueness of the minimal prime inside each maximal ideal.

standard_prerequisites.name: Henselian pairs, connectedness of V(q) with V of the maximal ideal, and profiniteness of the fibre over the residue field
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the unique maximal ideal containing a given minimal prime, which is the second half of part (3).

standard_prerequisites.name: Separability of the residue field extension and the bijection between Hom into the algebraic closure and the spectrum of a tensor product of fields
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the identification in part (1) of the fibre with Hom_kappa(kappa', kappa-bar).

core_obligations: Remove nilpotents: since (A/I)^{sh} = A^{sh}/IA^{sh} and the spectra of A, A^{sh}, A' and (A')^{sh} agree with those of the corresponding reduced rings, replace A by A_red and assume A is reduced, so that A is contained in A' (proof lines 31364-31373).

Part (1): note that kappa'/kappa is algebraic because A' is integral over A, use going up to see that every maximal ideal of A' or (A')^{sh} lies over the maximal ideal of A or A^{sh}, and compute (A')^{sh} tensor_{A^{sh}} kappa^{sep} = (A' tensor_A kappa) tensor_kappa kappa^{sep} (proof lines 31376-31390).

Part (1), conclusion: conclude that the fibre of c over m' is the spectrum of kappa' tensor_kappa kappa^{sep}, and that this spectrum is in bijection with Hom_kappa(kappa', kappa-bar) by sending sigma to the kernel of sigma tensor 1; note also that this spectrum is profinite because the ring is integral over a field (proof lines 31389-31396 and following).

Part (3): use that A' is a finite product of normal domains and that (A')^{sh}, being a filtered colimit of etale A'-algebras, is normal; conclude that every local ring of (A')^{sh} is a normal domain, so every maximal ideal contains a unique minimal prime (proof lines 31399-31411).

Part (3), conclusion: apply the integral-over-henselian-pair lemma to see ((A')^{sh}, m(A')^{sh}) is a henselian pair, use the connectedness lemma to see the intersection of V(q) with V(m (A')^{sh}) is connected for any prime q, and use that V(m (A')^{sh}) = Spec((A')^{sh} tensor kappa^{sh}) is profinite to obtain the unique maximal ideal containing q (proof lines 31411-31422).

Part (2): observe that the minimal primes of A' are exactly those over minimal primes of A, that flatness of A' -> (A')^{sh} plus quasi-finiteness of the filtered colimit shows every minimal prime of (A')^{sh} lies over a minimal prime of A', and similarly for A^{sh} (proof lines 31425-31433).

Part (2), conclusion: use A' tensor_A Q(A) = Q(A) with Q(A) the total fraction ring, a finite product of residue fields of the minimal primes of A, to get (A')^{sh} tensor_A Q(A) = A^{sh} tensor_A Q(A); identify the spectra of these two rings as the minimal primes of (A')^{sh} and of A^{sh} respectively, concluding that the right arrow is bijective on minimal primes (proof lines 31433-31450).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a local ring (A, m, kappa) with finitely many minimal primes, lets A' be the integral closure of A in the total ring of fractions of A_red, and considers the maps Spec(A') <- Spec((A')^{sh}) -> Spec(A^{sh}) where (A')^{sh} = A' tensor_A A^{sh}, the strict henselization being taken with respect to a separable algebraic closure kappa^{sep} of kappa inside an algebraic closure; it then asserts three things: that for a maximal ideal m' of A' the residue field kappa' is algebraic over kappa and the fibre of c over m' can be canonically identified with Hom_kappa(kappa', kappa-bar); that the right arrow is bijective on minimal primes; and that every minimal prime of (A')^{sh} lies in a unique maximal ideal and every maximal ideal contains a unique minimal prime (source lines 31338-31362). The proof first removes nilpotents: since (A/I)^{sh} = A^{sh}/IA^{sh} for the ideal I of nilpotents and the spectra involved agree, one may assume A is reduced (proof lines 31364-31373). Part (1) is then a computation: kappa'/kappa is algebraic because A' is integral over A, and by going up every maximal ideal of A' or (A')^{sh} lies over the corresponding maximal ideal; the proof computes (A')^{sh} tensor_{A^{sh}} kappa^{sep} = (A' tensor_A kappa) tensor_kappa kappa^{sep}, so the fibre of c over m' is the spectrum of kappa' tensor_kappa kappa^{sep}, and that spectrum is in bijection with Hom_kappa(kappa', kappa-bar) via the map sending sigma to the kernel of sigma tensor 1 (proof lines 31376-31396). Part (3) argues that A' is a finite product of normal domains, that (A')^{sh} is a filtered colimit of etale A'-algebras and hence normal, so every local ring of (A')^{sh} is a normal domain and every maximal ideal contains a unique minimal prime; then the integral-over-henselian-pair lemma makes ((A')^{sh}, m(A')^{sh}) a henselian pair and the connectedness lemma shows the intersection of V(q) with V(m (A')^{sh}) is connected, while V(m (A')^{sh}) = Spec((A')^{sh} tensor kappa^{sh}) is profinite, giving the unique maximal ideal above q (proof lines 31399-31422). Part (2) compares minimal primes of A' with those over minimal primes of A, uses flatness and quasi-finiteness of the filtered colimit to identify them, and finishes with the computation (A')^{sh} tensor_A Q(A) = A^{sh} tensor_A Q(A), where Q(A) is the total fraction ring, observing that the spectra of these two rings are exactly the minimal primes of (A')^{sh} and of A^{sh} respectively (proof lines 31425-31450). The non-routine content is the fibre computation in part (1), the henselian-pair connectedness argument in part (3), and the two-sided minimal-prime comparison in part (2).
